scenes.text: Your login token isn't secret. Anyone can read it. Claude spotted this in your admin route.
A JWT is three chunks. The first two are just base sixty-four: encoded, not encrypted.
So what stops you making yourself admin? The signature: a fingerprint of those chunks, made with a secret only the server knows.
Change one letter and the fingerprint breaks, so the server rejects it. If it checks.
Your admin route never did. Claude added verification on every request, and took the email out of the payload.
